body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فيقول المؤلف رحمه الله: باب مخارج الحروف الباب في اللغة فرجة في ساتر يتوصل بها من داخل إلى خارج وبالعكس حقيقةً في المباني كباب الدار وحكما في المعاني كباب مخارج الحروف، وهو في الاصطلاح اسم لطائفة من الفن تشترك في بعض الأحكام وتتميز عن غيرها، وهو يعقد لما يحتاج لبيانه من العلم، فهذا العلم الذي هو علم الأداء من مسائله التي تحتاج إلى عقد باب مخارج الحروف، والحروف قد سبق تعريفها وهي يبٍحث فيها من أربعة أوجه، الوجه الأول: المخرج (مخرج الحرف)، والوجه الثاني الصفة التي يتصف بها الحرف،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the author (may God have mercy on him) says: "Chapter on the points of articulation of the letters." A bāb, in the language, is a gap in a barrier by which one passes from inside to outside and the reverse — literally so in buildings, as with the door of a house, and by extension in meanings, as with the "chapter" on the points of articulation of the letters. In technical usage it is a name for a group of topics within a discipline which share certain rulings and are marked off from others; and it is set up for whatever stands in need of exposition within the science. Now this science, which is the science of Qur'anic delivery, has among its topics ones that require a chapter on the points of articulation of the letters to be set up. The letters have already been defined, and they are examined from four aspects. The first aspect: the point of articulation (the point of articulation of the letter). The second aspect: the quality by which the letter is characterised,

flags.context: والحروف قد سبق تعريفها وهي يبٍحث فيها من أربعة أوجه
options: Read as يُبحث فيها, 'they are examined', as rendered here
Read as يَبحث فيها, 'he examines them'
Leave unresolved as a transcription defect
flags.note: The stored word يبٍحث carries a stray kasratan on the bāʾ, which is not a possible vocalisation. The passive reading is the natural one in context and has been used; the defect has not been corrected in body_ar, per house rule 11.

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

The Sheikh announces that the letters are examined from four aspects and the excerpt gives only the first two before breaking off mid-clause. The remaining two are not in the source; nothing has been supplied for them, and the English must not be read as a complete statement of his scheme.

The passage turns on the double sense of bāb — a physical door and a chapter of a book. The English keeps both senses visible; the wordplay does not carry over, and the Arabic should be shown alongside.
ʿilm al-adāʾ, rendered here 'the science of Qur'anic delivery', is the science of how the Qur'an is pronounced in recitation; it is the wider discipline of which tajwid is part.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.
